## The I() construct

`?formula` gives you insights into the way to structure generic formula objects in R.  The `I()` construct is a consistent and clear way in R's foundations to specify functional operations on variables.

## R and GMM

There are a number of packages for estimating GMM models in R.  `pgmm` does many of the most basic models, though Stata is the industry leader in this.  That said, there is a relatively new and highly customizable package for this: `pdynmc` which is [described here in a pdf vignette](https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/pdynmc/vignettes/pdynmc-intro.pdf).  What follows is a detailed example with a software guide.

# Software Guide and Example

A (hopefully) practical reference for estimating dynamic panel data (DPD) and generalized method of moments (GMM) models. It covers the full range of estimators discussed in the course, from basic difference GMM through slope-heterogeneity tests and nonlinear dynamic models. Where one environment handles something the other cannot, that is noted explicitly.

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
# ── Load packages ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
library(plm)
library(lme4)
library(dplyr)
library(kableExtra)
# panelvar, fixest used in specific sections; install via install.packages() if needed

# ── Critical: restore plm::lag for pgmm formula parsing ───────────────────
# dplyr masks lag() with a version that rejects vector k (e.g. 1:2).
# Setting lag <- plm::lag here makes pgmm() formulas work globally.
# IMPORTANT: use dplyr::lag() explicitly in any dplyr pipeline — plm::lag
# applied to a plain vector inside mutate() returns the input unchanged,
# not a positional lag.
lag <- plm::lag

# ── Load and transform data ────────────────────────────────────────────────
data(EmplUK)
EmplUK <- EmplUK |>
  mutate(
    n  = log(emp),
    w  = log(wage),
    k  = log(capital),
    ys = log(output)
  )
pdat <- pdata.frame(EmplUK, index = c("firm", "year"))

# Precompute lag columns for plm(model = "random") formulas.
# Using lag() in a RE formula with lag <- plm::lag causes swar_Between_check()
# to fail (between-transform of lagged DV ≈ between-transform of level →
# singular between variance matrix). Precomputed columns sidestep this.
pdat$n_lag1 <- plm::lag(pdat$n, 1)
pdat$n_lag2 <- plm::lag(pdat$n, 2)
pdat$w_lag1 <- plm::lag(pdat$w, 1)

# ── Panel variance decomposition utility ───────────────────────────────────
panel_summary <- function(x, id) {
  grand  <- mean(x, na.rm = TRUE)
  btw    <- tapply(x, id, mean, na.rm = TRUE)
  within <- x - btw[as.character(id)]
  c(
    Grand_mean    = round(grand, 3),
    SD_total      = round(sd(x,      na.rm = TRUE), 3),
    SD_between    = round(sd(btw,    na.rm = TRUE), 3),
    SD_within     = round(sd(within, na.rm = TRUE), 3),
    Pct_within    = round(100 * var(within, na.rm=TRUE) / var(x, na.rm=TRUE), 1)
  )
}
```

This page is a practical reference for estimating dynamic panel data (DPD) and
generalized method of moments (GMM) models. It covers the full range of estimators
discussed in the course, from basic difference GMM through slope-heterogeneity tests
and nonlinear dynamic models. Where one environment handles something the other
cannot, that is noted explicitly.

## Package and command ecosystem

### R packages

Install once; load at the top of each script.

```{r packages, eval=FALSE}
install.packages(c(
  "plm",             # core panel estimators: pgmm, pmg, pcdtest
  "panelvar",        # panel VAR with impulse responses
  "lme4",            # mixed models for nonlinear DPD (CRE logit, Poisson)
  "fixest",          # fast FE Poisson and high-dimensional FE
  "marginaleffects", # average partial effects from nonlinear models
  "dplyr",           # data manipulation (also in tidyverse)
  "kableExtra"       # formatted output tables
))
```

::: {.callout-important}
## The `lag()` conflict between `plm` and `dplyr`

`dplyr` exports `lag()` with a scalar-only `n` argument. `plm` exports `lag()` that
accepts vector ranges like `1:2`, which `pgmm()` formulas require. Loading both
packages without intervention causes:

```
Error in lag(): ! n must be a whole number, not an integer vector.
```

**Fix**: add `lag <- plm::lag` once after loading both packages. This is done in
the hidden setup chunk for this document.

**Separate issue**: `plm::lag` applied to a plain numeric vector inside
`dplyr::mutate()` returns the input **unchanged** — it does not compute a
positional lag. Always use `dplyr::lag()` explicitly in pipeline code:

```r
df |> group_by(id) |> mutate(y_lag = dplyr::lag(y, 1))  # correct
df |> group_by(id) |> mutate(y_lag = lag(y, 1))          # wrong when lag <- plm::lag
```
:::

### Stata commands

Built-in commands ship with Stata. Community-contributed commands must be
installed once via `ssc install`.

```stata
* ---------- built-in commands ----------
* xtabond      Arellano-Bond difference GMM (one- or two-step)
* xtdpdsys     System GMM (Arellano-Bover / Blundell-Bond)
* xtdpd        General DPD — most flexible built-in specification
* xtregar      AR(1) FE/RE (not GMM; included for comparison)
* xtivreg      Panel IV (not full GMM)
* xtprobit     Random-effects probit
* xtpoisson    Random-effects Poisson / fixed-effects Poisson
* xtset id year  -- always declare panel structure first

* ---------- community commands (install once) ----------
ssc install xtabond2    // Roodman (2009): collapse, orthog. devs., diff-in-Hansen
ssc install xtlsdvc     // Bruno (2005): bias-corrected LSDV
ssc install xtpmg       // Pesaran-Shin-Smith (1999): MG and PMG estimators
ssc install xtdcce2     // Ditzen (2021): dynamic CCE
ssc install xtcd2       // Ditzen (2021): Pesaran CD test
ssc install xtslope     // Eberhardt (2012): Pesaran-Yamagata slope homogeneity
ssc install panelhet    // alternative slope homogeneity tests
ssc install pvar        // Abrigo-Love (2016): panel VAR
ssc install ivreg2      // extended IV/GMM (often needed alongside xtabond2)
```

## Data preparation

Both environments use the Layard-Nickell UK manufacturing employment data
(`abdata` in Stata; `EmplUK` in the `plm` package).

::: {.panel-tabset}

### R

```{r data-r}
library(plm)
library(dplyr)
data(EmplUK)

# Log-transform and declare panel structure
EmplUK <- EmplUK |>
  mutate(n = log(emp), w = log(wage), k = log(capital), ys = log(output))
pdat <- pdata.frame(EmplUK, index = c("firm", "year"))

# Set lag <- plm::lag for pgmm formula parsing (done in setup; shown here
# so the code is explicit when copying chunks to a standalone script)
lag <- plm::lag

# Precompute lag columns used by plm(model = "random") formulas.
# These must live in pdat so they are available to static-r.
# (Using lag() inside a RE formula with lag <- plm::lag causes
# swar_Between_check() to fail; precomputed columns avoid this.)
pdat$n_lag1 <- plm::lag(pdat$n, 1)
pdat$n_lag2 <- plm::lag(pdat$n, 2)
pdat$w_lag1 <- plm::lag(pdat$w, 1)

pdim(pdat)   # panel dimensions: N, T, balanced?
```

### Stata

```stata
use abdata, clear   // ships with Stata; n w k ys already logged

xtset id year       // declare panel structure; always do this first
xtdescribe          // shows panel balance / gaps
xtsum n w k ys      // within / between / overall variance decomposition
```

:::

::: {.panel-tabset}

### R

```{r variance-decomp}
# panel_summary() defined in the setup chunk; apply to each log variable
result <- sapply(c("n","w","k","ys"), function(v)
  panel_summary(EmplUK[[v]], EmplUK$firm))
t(result) |>
  kbl(caption = "Variance decomposition: 140 UK firms, 1976-1984") |>
  kable_styling(font_size = 13)
```

### Stata

```stata
xtsum n w k ys
```

:::

## Static panel baseline (for comparison)

Always estimate pooled OLS and fixed effects before GMM. They bracket the true
$\gamma$: OLS is upward-biased (omitted $\alpha_i$); FE is downward-biased
(Nickell). GMM estimates should lie between them.

::: {.panel-tabset}

### R

```{r static-r}
# Use precomputed lag columns (n_lag1, n_lag2, w_lag1 from setup).
# Avoids swar_Between_check() failure that occurs when lag <- plm::lag is
# active and lag() appears inside a random-effects formula.

# Pooled OLS (upward-biased gamma)
ols <- plm(n ~ n_lag1 + n_lag2 + w + w_lag1 + k + ys,
           data = pdat, model = "pooling")

# Two-way fixed effects (downward Nickell bias)
fe  <- plm(n ~ n_lag1 + n_lag2 + w + w_lag1 + k + ys,
           data = pdat, model = "within", effect = "twoways")

# Random effects — individual effects only.
# Two-way RE with a lagged DV is numerically fragile (Swamy-Arora
# between-estimator fails when between-transform of lag(n) ≈ between-transform
# of n itself). Individual RE is the sensible baseline comparison.
re  <- plm(n ~ n_lag1 + n_lag2 + w + w_lag1 + k + ys,
           data = pdat, model = "random", effect = "individual")

# Hausman test: FE vs RE
phtest(fe, re)

summary(fe)
```

### Stata

```stata
* Pooled OLS
reg n L(1/2).n w L.w k ys i.year

* Two-way fixed effects
xtreg n L(1/2).n w L.w k ys i.year, fe

* Random effects (individual only — see note on two-way RE above)
xtreg n L(1/2).n w L.w k ys, re

* Hausman test
estimates store re_est
xtreg n L(1/2).n w L.w k ys i.year, fe
hausman . re_est
```

:::

## Anderson-Hsiao: IV estimator

Anderson and Hsiao (1981) first-difference to remove fixed effects, then
instrument $\Delta y_{i,t-1}$ with $y_{i,t-2}$ (level) or $\Delta y_{i,t-2}$
(difference). Useful pedagogically as the conceptual predecessor to AB.

::: {.panel-tabset}

### R

```{r ah-r}
# First-difference by hand.
# MUST use dplyr::lag() explicitly here — plm::lag() on a plain vector
# inside mutate() returns the input unchanged, not a positional lag.
pdat_fd <- EmplUK |>
  group_by(firm) |> arrange(year) |>
  mutate(
    Dn   = n  - dplyr::lag(n, 1),       # Delta y_t
    DLn  = dplyr::lag(n,1) - dplyr::lag(n,2),  # Delta y_{t-1}  (endogenous)
    Dw   = w  - dplyr::lag(w, 1),
    ln2  = dplyr::lag(n, 2),             # y_{t-2}: level instrument
    DLn2 = dplyr::lag(n,2) - dplyr::lag(n,3)   # Delta y_{t-2}: diff instrument
  ) |>
  ungroup() |> filter(!is.na(DLn2))

pdat_fd_p <- pdata.frame(pdat_fd, index = c("firm","year"))

# AH estimator using plm() IV formula syntax: y ~ endog | instruments
# Level instrument y_{t-2}
ah_level <- plm(Dn ~ DLn + Dw | ln2  + Dw, data = pdat_fd_p, model = "pooling")
summary(ah_level)

# Difference instrument Delta y_{t-2}
ah_diff  <- plm(Dn ~ DLn + Dw | DLn2 + Dw, data = pdat_fd_p, model = "pooling")
summary(ah_diff)
```

### Stata

```stata
* First-difference; instrument with lagged level y_{t-2}
ivregress 2sls D.n (D.L.n = L2.n) D.w, vce(robust)

* Instrument with lagged difference Delta y_{t-2}
ivregress 2sls D.n (D.L.n = LD.n) D.w, vce(robust)

* ivreg2 gives first-stage F, Cragg-Donald, Kleibergen-Paap weak instrument tests
ivreg2 D.n (D.L.n = L2.n) D.w, robust first
```

:::

---

## Arellano-Bond: difference GMM

Arellano and Bond (1991) use all valid lagged levels as GMM instruments.
The global `lag <- plm::lag` (set in the setup chunk) makes `pgmm()` formulas
work correctly throughout.

### Formula syntax for `pgmm()`

Left of `|`: model covariates with lag structure. Right of `|`: GMM-type
instruments via `lag(var, min:max)`, where `2:99` means all available lags
from 2 onward.

### One-step Arellano-Bond

::: {.panel-tabset}

### R

```{r ab1-r}
# Replicates Arellano-Bond (1991) Table 4(a1)
# lag() resolves to plm::lag (set globally in setup) -- pgmm formulas work
ab_one <- pgmm(
  log(emp) ~ lag(log(emp), 1:2) +
             lag(log(wage), 0:1) +
             lag(log(capital), 0:2) +
             lag(log(output), 0:2) |
             lag(log(emp), 2:99),
  data   = EmplUK,
  effect = "twoways",
  model  = "onestep"
)
summary(ab_one)
```

### Stata

```stata
* Built-in command
xtabond n L(0/1).w L(0/2).(k ys) yr1980-yr1984, lags(2) vce(robust)
estat abond
estat sargan

* xtabond2 — generally preferred
xtabond2 n L(1/2).n L(0/1).w L(0/2).(k ys) yr1980-yr1984,     ///
    gmm(L.n, lag(2 99))                                          ///
    iv(L(0/1).w L(0/2).(k ys) yr1980-yr1984)                    ///
    twostep robust small
```

:::

### Two-step with Windmeijer-corrected standard errors

::: {.panel-tabset}

### R

```{r ab2-r}
# Replicates AB (1991) Table 4(b)
ab_two <- pgmm(
  log(emp) ~ lag(log(emp), 1:2) +
             lag(log(wage), 0:1) +
             log(capital) +
             lag(log(output), 0:1) |
             lag(log(emp), 2:99),
  data   = EmplUK,
  effect = "twoways",
  model  = "twosteps"
)

# robust = TRUE applies Windmeijer (2005) correction — always use this
summary(ab_two, robust = TRUE)

# Compare naive two-step SEs (too small) vs Windmeijer
summary(ab_two, robust = FALSE)
```

### Stata

```stata
xtabond n L(0/1).w k L(0/1).ys yr1980-yr1984, lags(2) twostep vce(robust)

xtabond2 n L(1/2).n L(0/1).w k L(0/1).ys yr1980-yr1984,        ///
    gmm(L.n, lag(2 99))                                          ///
    iv(L(0/1).w k L(0/1).ys yr1980-yr1984)                      ///
    twostep robust small
```

:::

### Instrument management: lag depth and collapsing

::: {.panel-tabset}

### R

```{r instr-r}
# Limit lag depth: lags 2 through 4 only
ab_limited <- pgmm(
  log(emp) ~ lag(log(emp), 1:2) + lag(log(wage), 0:1) +
             log(capital) + lag(log(output), 0:1) |
             lag(log(emp), 2:4),
  data = EmplUK, effect = "twoways", model = "twosteps"
)
summary(ab_limited, robust = TRUE)

# Instrument count: Sargan df = L - K
cat("Instruments:", length(ab_limited$coefficients) + ab_limited$df.residual, "\n")
cat("Groups (firms):", pdim(pdat)$nT$n, "\n")
```

**R limitation**: `plm::pgmm()` does not support instrument collapsing. Use
`xtabond2` in Stata for the `collapse` option.

### Stata

```stata
* Limit lag depth
xtabond2 n L(1/2).n L(0/1).w k L(0/1).ys yr1980-yr1984,        ///
    gmm(L.n, lag(2 4))                                           ///
    iv(L(0/1).w k L(0/1).ys yr1980-yr1984)                      ///
    twostep robust small

* Collapse instrument matrix (reduces O(T^2) to O(T) instruments)
xtabond2 n L(1/2).n L(0/1).w k L(0/1).ys yr1980-yr1984,        ///
    gmm(L.n, lag(2 99) collapse)                                 ///
    iv(L(0/1).w k L(0/1).ys yr1980-yr1984)                      ///
    twostep robust small
```

:::

---

## System GMM: Arellano-Bover / Blundell-Bond

::: {.panel-tabset}

### R

```{r bb-r}
# Replicates Blundell-Bond (1998) Table 4
# transformation = "ld" stacks levels + differences
bb <- pgmm(
  log(emp) ~ lag(log(emp), 1) +
             lag(log(wage), 0:1) +
             lag(log(capital), 0:1) |
             lag(log(emp), 2:99) +
             lag(log(wage), 2:99) +
             lag(log(capital), 2:99),
  data           = EmplUK,
  effect         = "twoways",
  model          = "onestep",
  transformation = "ld"
)
summary(bb, robust = TRUE)
```

### Stata

```stata
* Built-in system GMM command
xtdpdsys n L(0/1).w L(0/1).k yr1980-yr1984, lags(1) twostep vce(robust)
estat abond
estat sargan

* xtabond2 (preferred — adds collapse, orthogonal, diff-in-Hansen)
xtabond2 n L.n L(0/1).w L(0/1).k yr1980-yr1984,                 ///
    gmm(L.n, lag(2 99) collapse)                                 ///
    gmm(L.w L.k, lag(2 99) collapse)                             ///
    iv(yr1980-yr1984)                                            ///
    twostep robust small

* xtdpd: most general, requires explicit instrument specification
xtdpd n L(1/2).n L(0/1).w L(0/1).k yr1980-yr1984,              ///
    dgmmiv(n, lagrange(2 99)) lgmmiv(n) iv(yr1980-yr1984)       ///
    twostep vce(robust)
```

:::

## Post-estimation: specification tests

### Arellano-Bond serial correlation tests

::: {.panel-tabset}

### R

```{r ar-tests-r}
# ab_two created in the ab2-r chunk above
mtest(ab_two, order = 1)   # should reject (mechanical from differencing)
mtest(ab_two, order = 2)   # should NOT reject — key identification check
```

### Stata

```stata
estat abond              // after xtabond, xtdpdsys, xtdpd
estat abond, lags(3)     // extend to AR(3) if needed
```

:::

### Sargan / Hansen overidentification test

::: {.panel-tabset}

### R

```{r sargan-r}
# summary() prints Sargan/Hansen automatically
s1 <- summary(ab_one)              # Sargan (one-step, non-robust)
s2 <- summary(ab_two, robust=TRUE) # Hansen J (two-step, Windmeijer)

# Extract the statistic directly
cat("One-step Sargan:  statistic =", round(s1$sargan$statistic, 2),
    " df =", s1$sargan$parameter,
    " p =", round(s1$sargan$p.value, 3), "\n")
cat("Two-step Hansen:  statistic =", round(s2$sargan$statistic, 2),
    " df =", s2$sargan$parameter,
    " p =", round(s2$sargan$p.value, 3), "\n")
```

### Stata

```stata
estat sargan       // after xtabond / xtdpdsys / xtdpd
                   // xtabond2 prints Hansen automatically
```

:::

### Difference-in-Hansen test

::: {.panel-tabset}

### R

```{r dih-r}
# Not implemented in plm::pgmm() or any current CRAN package.
# This test is only available via xtabond2 in Stata.
message("Difference-in-Hansen test: use xtabond2 in Stata (see Stata tab).")
```

### Stata

```stata
* xtabond2 computes difference-in-Hansen automatically when multiple
* gmm() blocks are specified — tests each instrument subset separately
xtabond2 n L.n L(0/1).w L(0/1).k yr1980-yr1984,                 ///
    gmm(L.n,         lag(2 99) collapse)                         ///
    gmm(L(0/1).w L(0/1).k, lag(2 99) collapse)                  ///
    iv(yr1980-yr1984)                                            ///
    twostep robust small
* Output: "Difference-in-Hansen tests of exogeneity of instrument subsets"
```

:::

## Bias-corrected LSDV (LSDVC)

::: {.panel-tabset}

### R

```{r lsdvc-r}
# LSDVC (Bruno 2005) has no maintained CRAN implementation.
# Best approach in R: triangulate FE (lower bound) and AB (consistent).
fe_est <- plm(n ~ n_lag1 + n_lag2 + w + w_lag1 + k + ys,
              data = pdat, model = "within", effect = "twoways")
ab_est <- pgmm(
  log(emp) ~ lag(log(emp),1:2) + lag(log(wage),0:1) +
             log(capital) | lag(log(emp),2:4),
  data = EmplUK, effect = "twoways", model = "twosteps"
)

cat("FE  gamma1:", round(coef(fe_est)["n_lag1"], 4), " [downward-biased]\n")
cat("AB  gamma1:", round(coef(ab_est)[1],        4), " [consistent]\n")
cat("LSDVC lies between these; use xtlsdvc in Stata for the bias-corrected point estimate\n")
```

**R limitation**: Bruno (2005) LSDVC is Stata-only. Use `xtlsdvc` for the
actual bias-corrected estimate.

### Stata

```stata
* initial() options: ah, ab, bb
xtlsdvc n L.n L(0/1).w L(0/1).k yr1980-yr1984, initial(ab) vcov(500) lags(1)
xtlsdvc n L.n L(0/1).w L(0/1).k yr1980-yr1984, initial(bb) vcov(500) lags(1)

foreach init in ah ab bb {
    di "--- Initialization: `init' ---"
    xtlsdvc n L.n L(0/1).w L(0/1).k yr1980-yr1984, ///
        initial(`init') vcov(200) lags(1)
}
```

:::

## Unbalanced panels and orthogonal deviations

::: {.panel-tabset}

### R

```{r orthog-r, eval=FALSE}
library(panelvar)
# data(EmplUK)
if (!"n" %in% names(EmplUK)) EmplUK$n <- log(EmplUK$emp)

# pvargmm() looks up column names literally; "n" must exist in data
pvgmm_fod <- pvargmm(
  dependent_vars           = c("n"),
  lags                     = 1,
  transformation           = "fod",    # forward orthogonal deviations
  data                     = EmplUK,
  panel_identifier         = c("firm", "year"),
  steps                    = "twosteps",
  system_instruments       = FALSE,
  max_instr_dependent_vars = 4,
  min_instr_dependent_vars = 2
)
summary(pvgmm_fod)
```

**R limitation**: `plm::pgmm()` does not support orthogonal deviations.
Use `panelvar::pvargmm()` with `transformation = "fod"`.

### Stata

```stata
xtabond2 n L.n L(0/1).w L(0/1).k yr1980-yr1984,                 ///
    gmm(L.n, lag(2 99) collapse)                                 ///
    iv(L(0/1).w L(0/1).k yr1980-yr1984)                         ///
    twostep robust small                                         ///
    orthogonal
```

:::

## Panel VAR

::: {.panel-tabset}

### R

```{r pvar-r, eval=FALSE}
library(panelvar)
# data(EmplUK)
EmplUK$n <- log(EmplUK$emp)
EmplUK$w <- log(EmplUK$wage)

# Panel VAR: employment and wages jointly endogenous
# Use transformation = "fod" to handle EmplUK's unbalanced structure
pvar_mod <- pvargmm(
  dependent_vars           = c("n", "w"),
  lags                     = 1,
  transformation           = "fod",
  data                     = EmplUK,
  panel_identifier         = c("firm", "year"),
  steps                    = "twosteps",
  system_instruments       = FALSE,
  max_instr_dependent_vars = 4,
  min_instr_dependent_vars = 2
)
summary(pvar_mod)

# Stability: characteristic roots inside unit circle
stability(pvar_mod)

# Generalised impulse response functions
pvar_irf <- girf(pvar_mod, n.ahead = 8, ma_approx_steps = 8)
plot(pvar_irf)
```

### Stata

```stata
* ssc install pvar
pvar n w, lags(1) fod twostep
pvarstable
pvarirf, oirf mc(500) step(8)
pvargranger
```

:::

**Software note**: R's `panelvar` provides richer IRF, stability diagnostics,
and forecast-error variance decomposition than Stata's `pvar`. Point estimates
are comparable.

## Slope heterogeneity: testing and estimation

### Step 1: Cross-sectional dependence

::: {.panel-tabset}

### R

```{r cd-test-r}
# Fit a baseline FE model, then test residuals for cross-sectional dependence
fe_cd <- plm(n ~ n_lag1 + n_lag2 + w + w_lag1 + k + ys,
             data = pdat, model = "within", effect = "twoways")
pcdtest(fe_cd, test = "cd")   # Pesaran (2015) CD test
pcdtest(fe_cd, test = "lm")   # LM version (better for small T)
```

### Stata

```stata
xtreg n L(1/2).n w L.w k ys i.year, fe
xtcd2   // Ditzen (2021); ssc install xtcd2
```

:::

### Step 2: Slope homogeneity test

::: {.panel-tabset}

### R

```{r slope-test-r}
# The formal Pesaran-Yamagata (2008) Delta-tilde test is not on CRAN.
# Approximation: run unit-by-unit OLS, inspect coefficient dispersion.
unit_coefs <- lapply(split(EmplUK, EmplUK$firm), function(d) {
  d <- d |> arrange(year) |>
    mutate(n_l1 = dplyr::lag(n,1), n_l2 = dplyr::lag(n,2),
           w_l1 = dplyr::lag(w,1)) |>
    filter(!is.na(n_l2))
  if (nrow(d) < 5) return(NULL)
  tryCatch(coef(lm(n ~ n_l1 + n_l2 + w + w_l1 + k + ys, data=d)),
           error = function(e) NULL)
})
unit_coefs <- do.call(rbind, Filter(Negate(is.null), unit_coefs))
cat("Coefficient of variation across units (informal heterogeneity check):\n")
round(apply(unit_coefs, 2, function(x) sd(x, na.rm=TRUE) /
              abs(mean(x, na.rm=TRUE))), 3)
```

**R limitation**: Use `xtslope` in Stata for the formal Pesaran-Yamagata
$\tilde\Delta$ test statistic with correct inference.

### Stata

```stata
* ssc install xtslope
xtslope n L.n w L.w k ys    // Delta and Delta-tilde statistics + p-values
```

:::

### Mean Group and Common Correlated Effects MG

::: {.panel-tabset}

### R

```{r mg-pmg-r}
# plm::pmg() supports: "mg" (Mean Group), "cmg" (CCE-MG), "dmg" (Demeaned MG)
# The Pooled Mean Group (PMG) estimator of Pesaran-Shin-Smith (1999) is
# NOT available in plm — use xtpmg in Stata for that.

mg_mod  <- pmg(n ~ w + k + ys, data = pdat, model = "mg")   # Mean Group
cmg_mod <- pmg(n ~ w + k + ys, data = pdat, model = "cmg")  # CCE Mean Group

summary(mg_mod)
summary(cmg_mod)

# Hausman-type test: MG vs CMG
# H0: common factors not needed (CMG = MG asymptotically)
# Rejection suggests unobserved common factors are important
phtest(mg_mod, cmg_mod)
```

**R note**: `plm::pmg(model = "cmg")` is the Common Correlated Effects MG
(Pesaran 2006) — it augments each unit regression with cross-sectional means.
Pooled Mean Group (Pesaran-Shin-Smith 1999) is only available via `xtpmg` in
Stata.

### Stata

```stata
* xtpmg: Pesaran-Shin-Smith (1999)
xtpmg d.n d.w d.k d.ys, lr(L.n w k ys) ec(ec_term) full mg
estimates store mg

xtpmg d.n d.w d.k d.ys, lr(L.n w k ys) ec(ec_term) full pmg
estimates store pmg

* Hausman: H0 = long-run slopes homogeneous (PMG efficient under H0)
hausman mg pmg, sigmamore
```

:::

### Dynamic CCE for cross-sectional dependence

::: {.panel-tabset}

### R

```{r dcce-r}
# Dynamic CCE via cross-sectional mean augmentation (manual CCE-MG).
# xtdcce2 is Stata-only; no equivalent on CRAN.
# This approximates CCE-MG but does not compute correct inferential SEs.

EmplUK_aug <- EmplUK |>
  group_by(year) |>
  mutate(
    n_bar  = mean(n,  na.rm = TRUE),
    w_bar  = mean(w,  na.rm = TRUE),
    k_bar  = mean(k,  na.rm = TRUE),
    ys_bar = mean(ys, na.rm = TRUE)
  ) |> ungroup()

# Unit-by-unit CCE-MG: augment each unit regression with cross-sectional means
ccemg_coefs <- lapply(split(EmplUK_aug, EmplUK_aug$firm), function(d) {
  d <- d |> arrange(year) |>
    mutate(n_l1 = dplyr::lag(n,1), n_l2 = dplyr::lag(n,2),
           w_l1 = dplyr::lag(w,1)) |>
    filter(!is.na(n_l2))
  if (nrow(d) < 5) return(NULL)
  tryCatch(
    coef(lm(n ~ n_l1 + n_l2 + w + w_l1 + k + ys +
              n_bar + w_bar + k_bar + ys_bar, data = d)),
    error = function(e) NULL)
})
ccemg_coefs <- do.call(rbind, Filter(Negate(is.null), ccemg_coefs))
cat("CCE-MG point estimates (SEs not valid — use xtdcce2 in Stata):\n")
round(colMeans(ccemg_coefs, na.rm = TRUE), 4)
```

**R limitation**: A production-quality DCCE estimator with correct SEs is not
on CRAN. Use `xtdcce2` in Stata.

### Stata

```stata
* ssc install xtdcce2
xtdcce2 n L.n w k ys, cr(n w k ys) cr_lags(1)     // pooled CCE
xtdcce2 n L.n w k ys, cr(n w k ys) cr_lags(1) mg  // CCE-MG (heterogeneous)
```

:::

## Nonlinear dynamic panel models: binary and count outcomes

### Data construction

::: {.panel-tabset}

### R

```{r nonlin-setup-r}
# Create a binary DV and compute Mundlak / Wooldridge (2005) terms.
# MUST use dplyr::lag() explicitly — plm::lag() on a plain vector
# inside mutate() does not compute a positional lag.
panel_df <- EmplUK |>
  mutate(n_hi = as.integer(n > median(n, na.rm = TRUE))) |>
  group_by(firm) |> arrange(year) |>
  mutate(
    n_hi_lag = dplyr::lag(n_hi, 1),   # lagged binary DV
    y_init   = first(n_hi),            # initial condition y_{i1}
    w_bar    = mean(w,  na.rm = TRUE), # unit mean of wage (Mundlak term)
    k_bar    = mean(k,  na.rm = TRUE)
  ) |>
  ungroup() |>
  filter(!is.na(n_hi_lag))

cat("Observations after setup:", nrow(panel_df), "\n")
cat("Binary DV mean:", round(mean(panel_df$n_hi), 3), "\n")
```

### Stata

```stata
xtile n_hi = n, nq(2)
replace n_hi = (n_hi == 2)

bysort id (year): gen y_init = n_hi[1]
bysort id: egen w_bar = mean(w)
bysort id: egen k_bar = mean(k)
```

:::

### Dynamic logit: Wooldridge (2005) CRE approach

Wooldridge (2005) conditions on the initial value $y_{i1}$ to proxy the
distribution of $\alpha_i$, yielding a standard RE logit (or probit)
augmented with $y_{i1}$ and unit-means $\bar{x}_i$ as additional covariates.
Logit is used here rather than probit for numerical stability; the approach
and interpretation are identical.

::: {.panel-tabset}

### R

```{r dynlogit-r}
library(lme4)

# Wooldridge (2005) CRE dynamic logit
# y_init proxies distribution of alpha_i; w_bar, k_bar are Mundlak terms
mod_logit <- glmer(
  n_hi ~ n_hi_lag + w + k + y_init + w_bar + k_bar + (1 | firm),
  data    = panel_df,
  family  = binomial(link = "logit"),
  control = glmerControl(optimizer = "bobyqa", optCtrl = list(maxfun = 2e5))
)
summary(mod_logit)

# Average Partial Effects (APEs) — interpret these, not the latent coefficients
# Requires marginaleffects package:
# avg_slopes(mod_logit, variables = c("n_hi_lag","w","k"), re.form = NA)

# Test: is initial condition significant? Confirms initial-conditions problem.
cat("\nWald test for y_init (psi_1 != 0):\n")
print(car::linearHypothesis(mod_logit, "y_init = 0"))
```

### Stata

```stata
* RE probit (Stata convention; probit and logit give equivalent inferences)
xtprobit n_hi L.n_hi w k y_init w_bar k_bar, re

* APEs
margins, dydx(L.n_hi w k) predict(pu0)

* Test initial condition
test y_init

* RE logit
xtlogit n_hi L.n_hi w k y_init w_bar k_bar, re
margins, dydx(L.n_hi w k) predict(pr)
```

:::

### Dynamic Poisson / count models

::: {.panel-tabset}

### R

```{r dynpois-r, eval=FALSE}
# CRE Poisson: Wooldridge (2005) / Blundell-Griffith-Windmeijer (2002) approach
# Use emp (count) as outcome; include y_init as initial-condition control
pois_df <- EmplUK |>
  group_by(firm) |> arrange(year) |>
  mutate(
    emp_lag = dplyr::lag(emp, 1),
    y_init  = first(emp),
    w_bar   = mean(w, na.rm = TRUE),
    k_bar   = mean(k, na.rm = TRUE)
  ) |>
  ungroup() |> filter(!is.na(emp_lag))

mod_pois <- glmer(
  emp ~ emp_lag + w + k + y_init + w_bar + k_bar + (1 | firm),
  data    = pois_df,
  family  = poisson,
  control = glmerControl(optimizer = "bobyqa")
)
summary(mod_pois)

# FE Poisson via fixest (consistent, no incidental-parameters bias for Poisson)
# library(fixest)
# fe_pois <- fepois(emp ~ emp_lag + w + k | firm + year, data = pois_df)
```

### Stata

```stata
* CRE Poisson
xtpoisson emp L.emp w k y_init w_bar k_bar, re
margins, dydx(*) predict(nu0)

* FE Poisson (Hausman-Hall-Griliches 1984 — no incidental-parameters problem)
xtpoisson emp L.emp w k, fe
```

:::

## Capability matrix

| Estimator / Feature | R (`plm`) | R (other) | Stata built-in | Stata (`ssc`) |
|---|:---:|:---:|:---:|:---:|
| Anderson-Hsiao IV | `plm` IV formula | — | `ivregress` | `ivreg2` |
| AB one-step diff. GMM | ✅ `pgmm` | `panelvar` | `xtabond` | `xtabond2` |
| AB two-step + Windmeijer | ✅ `pgmm` | `panelvar` | `xtabond` | `xtabond2` |
| System GMM (BB) | ✅ `pgmm(ld)` | `panelvar` | `xtdpdsys` | `xtabond2` |
| Collapse instrument matrix | ❌ | Partial `panelvar` | ❌ | ✅ `xtabond2` |
| Orthogonal deviations | ❌ | ✅ `panelvar` | ❌ | ✅ `xtabond2` |
| Difference-in-Hansen test | ❌ | ❌ | ❌ | ✅ `xtabond2` |
| Sargan / Hansen $J$-test | ✅ `summary(pgmm)` | — | `estat sargan` | ✅ `xtabond2` |
| Arellano-Bond AR tests | ✅ `mtest()` | — | `estat abond` | ✅ `xtabond2` |
| LSDVC (Bruno 2005) | ❌ | ❌ CRAN | ❌ | ✅ `xtlsdvc` |
| Panel VAR + IRFs | — | ✅ `panelvar` | ❌ | ✅ `pvar` |
| Pesaran CD test | ✅ `pcdtest()` | — | ❌ | ✅ `xtcd2` |
| Pesaran-Yamagata $\tilde\Delta$ | Manual only | ❌ CRAN | ❌ | ✅ `xtslope` |
| Mean Group (MG) | ✅ `pmg("mg")` | — | ❌ | ✅ `xtpmg` |
| CCE Mean Group (CMG) | ✅ `pmg("cmg")` | — | ❌ | ✅ `xtdcce2 mg` |
| Pooled Mean Group (PMG) | ❌ | ❌ | ❌ | ✅ `xtpmg` |
| Dynamic CCE (`xtdcce2`) | Manual (no SEs) | ❌ CRAN | ❌ | ✅ `xtdcce2` |
| CRE dynamic logit | ✅ `lme4::glmer` | — | ✅ `xtlogit,re` | — |
| CRE dynamic probit | ✅ `lme4::glmer` | — | ✅ `xtprobit,re` | — |
| CRE Poisson | ✅ `lme4::glmer` | ✅ `fixest::fepois` | ✅ `xtpoisson,re` | — |
| FE Poisson (H-H-G) | — | ✅ `fixest::fepois` | ✅ `xtpoisson,fe` | — |
| Average partial effects | ✅ `marginaleffects` | — | ✅ `margins` | — |

**Legend**: ✅ well-supported; Partial = implemented but less complete; Manual =
user code required, inference not automatic; ❌ not available.

---

## Key cross-software notes

**`xtabond2` is the recommended Stata command** for nearly all GMM DPD work.
It supersedes `xtabond`, `xtdpdsys`, and `xtdpd` and is the only command
with collapsed instruments, orthogonal deviations, and difference-in-Hansen.

**`plm::pgmm()` is the R workhorse** but has three hard gaps: no collapsed
instruments, no orthogonal deviations, no difference-in-Hansen. For panels
where these matter, call `xtabond2` via Stata.

**LSDVC and PMG belong to Stata**. Bruno (2005) bias-corrected LSDV
(`xtlsdvc`) and Pesaran-Shin-Smith (1999) Pooled Mean Group (`xtpmg`) have
no maintained CRAN implementations.

**Slope heterogeneity diagnostics are Stata-favoured**. The formal
Pesaran-Yamagata $\tilde\Delta$ test (`xtslope`) and Dynamic CCE (`xtdcce2`)
have no direct CRAN equivalents. `plm::pmg(model = "cmg")` provides CCE-MG
estimation but without the full DCCE workflow.

**Nonlinear DPD is well-handled in both** environments via the Wooldridge
(2005) CRE approach. `lme4::glmer()` in R and `xtlogit/xtprobit/xtpoisson, re`
in Stata implement the same estimator. Use `marginaleffects::avg_slopes()` in
R and `margins` in Stata for average partial effects — always report APEs, not
latent-index coefficients.
